name: 系统工具
description: The api/system surface: question-bank CRUD, system_settings, the operation-log reader and the whole-database backup export. Adopts question_bank and system_settings; everything else it touches is declared read access. Migrated out of api/modules/system (P4.3b.5).

data._adopted_note: question_bank is this domain's own resource (challenge reads it, admin deletes it during a class purge - both are declared readers/writers elsewhere, not co-owners). system_settings is a KNOWN ownership debt: this plugin serves GET/POST /api/system/settings, but the *live* admin endpoint `GET|PUT /api/admin/system/settings` writes the same table through Prisma (api/modules/admin/admin.repository.ts:669-691) with its own canonical key list in admin.defaults.ts. Nothing on the frontend calls /api/system/settings, so the honest resolution is for admin to own this table and for these two routes to disappear with it - deleting a route is a surface change, so it is deliberately left for the round that migrates admin. Recorded here rather than silently left implicit.
data._reads_note: Sixteen tables, all read-only, and all of them exist in api/schema/legacyBootSchema.ts (checked against the boot DDL). Fifteen are there for GET /api/system/backup/export, which dumps whole tables that belong to other domains - see BACKUP_TABLES in src/system.repository.ts; `settings` is dumped there too. operation_logs is the sixteenth: the kernel's audit sink owns that table (migration 0005_kernel_operation_logs), so GET /api/system/logs reads it and can never write it. A backup export that spans domains is inherently a platform concern; when the remaining domains migrate this should become a kernel-side registry of dumpable tables rather than a static list here.
